name: Petunia
lede: Petunia is a very dark purple, named for the garden flower.

sections.title: A garden flower's color
sections.body:
Paterson's one-line definition is a dark purple [1]. He lists it with the purples, beside plum, prune and aubergine [2]. The books give no more: no dye, no date, no story [1][2].

Our library traces the name to Maerz and Paul's *Dictionary of Color* of 1930, plate 46, and to the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955, where the swatch falls in the very deep purple block [3]. The swatch is much darker than most petunia petals, so the name works here as a dark reddish purple [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #470659 is near-black, with a lightness of about 17 out of 100 [3]. No painting in our archive of 23,781 has it covering even 1% of the canvas, as photographed [4]. That is no surprise: such deep purples are usually shadows, not subjects, and pass for black in varnished photographs [4]. Near neighbors are [[plum]], [[aubergine]] and [[eggplant]] [3].
